$comment: What the platform takes from one order, as one table asserted by both engines.
The engine exists twice on purpose: `Revenue.takeFrom` in Dart decides what the
phone SHOWS, and `order_revenue_take` in Postgres decides what is actually TAKEN.
The server's answer is the one that counts, and the phone's is the one a merchant
reads off a screen before they hand over food — so the two disagreeing is not a
rounding curiosity, it is an argument in a shop with money on the counter.
Before this file the two sides were tested against different figures, which proves
each one self-consistent and nothing at all about them agreeing. A case added here
`supabase/test/local/settlement_arithmetic.test.js`, so a divergence fails a test
rather than turning up in somebody's till.
All figures are piastres. `value` is basis points under commission, piastres per
order under prepaid, and meaningless under subscription.

cases.why: subscription takes nothing, whatever the order was worth
and a value on a subscription snapshot changes nothing
rounded down, never to nearest: 12.34% of 99.99 EGP is 1233.87 piastres
rounded down again, on a figure that would round up
200% is a typo for 2.00%, and must not make a merchant owe double
a negative rate takes nothing rather than paying the merchant
prepaid is the flat fee, whatever the order was worth
and the same fee on an order twenty times the size
never more than the order: a fee that puts a merchant in the red on a small sale stops them taking small sales
an order worth nothing owes nothing, under commission
a negative basis is not a refund
